rules.why: Short entry after the price has already squeezed up since the signal and taker buying has faded. This catches the 'against_then_for' shape (MAE around 3h) after the adverse move is spent, so the entry is higher and the floor is further away.

Shorts on Bybit have been covering (the crowd shifted long) while price rose. This marks a short squeeze that has already happened; the forced buying is done, leaving a better price to short with less squeeze fuel left.

Open interest is unwinding during a rise after the signal. The rally is driven by liquidations or covering rather than new longs, so it tends to exhaust; entering after the unwind avoids the straight_against paths.

A burst of aggressive buying that ate through ask depth and lifted the price for an hour. This is a buying climax where exhaustion is likely, so shorting into it gives a better fill than entering at the signal.

Funding has turned positive and longs are paying while the price is at or above the signal price. Longs are getting crowded, and a short collects funding and gets in at a no-worse price than the signal.
Pump already happened (4h up >6%), buying burst has faded and OI is unwinding: late longs exiting, so shorting the exhausted top should lower adverse excursion versus entering at the signal hour.
Price ran against the signal (better short price), but taker flow has turned to selling and the crowd is not adding shorts. The squeeze risk is spent, so a 5% stop rarely hits the winners.
Positive funding means longs pay and are crowded. A 1h up-move on below-normal trade activity is a weak, thin rally, which makes a good fade entry for shorts.
Long-heavy crowd starts unwinding (OI falling, price turning down): a long liquidation cascade begins, so the short enters with momentum and little adverse excursion, which suits a tight 3% stop.

Price has already squeezed at least 2% against the short since the signal, and aggressive buying has dropped below half of trades. Entering here means the adverse leg is behind us, which should shrink the further adverse excursion so a 5% stop can survive.

A squeeze has taken place (price up 3% or more since the signal) and open interest is now unwinding. The shorts who were forced out have covered, so the fuel for further upside is spent. Waiting past the squeeze should make the remaining adverse move small enough for a 3% stop at equal risk.

Price rose after the signal and then printed the first down hour of at least 1%. Entering on that rollover sells near a local high, after the 'against then for' move has started, which should lower the adverse excursion.
Price is above the signal level, but trade-burst intensity has collapsed. The buying burst that lifted the price is exhausting, so the short is entered at a better price with momentum fading.
Longs are crowded and paying positive funding while price stalls or dips. Trapped longs who are bleeding funding tend to unwind, which favours the short with limited upside risk.

exit_rules.why: Coins that often hit the book's floor have large, fast losses. A 3% stop at equal risk cuts those losers early and still lets a 3x take capture the winners; this gain held in both halves.
Thin bid-side depth consumption at the signal means little aggressive pressure is present. Adverse moves tend to be contained, so a 3% stop rarely cuts winners; this gain held in both halves.
Wide-spread, illiquid names make noisy swings that tighter stops would cut. A wide 8% stop with a 3x take lets the larger moves play out; this gain held in both halves.
When BTC is already falling over 24h, the market tailwind supports the short. A wide stop is enough to cap a rare reversal without cutting the trend move; this gain held in both halves.
